title: Yellowed Fluffy Chinese Pork Char Siu Bao
description: A malty and fluffy Chinese dish featuring ground cinnamon and dashi extract, this sugar-free-friendly char siu bao is a delicious meal prep option. It is a traditional Shandong dish with a unique flavor profile.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the ground pork, ground cinnamon, dashi extract, and salt, and mix until just combined.
In a separate bowl, combine the wheat flour, instant yeast, and sesame oil, and mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces and roll each piece into a ball.
Flatten each ball into a disk and place a tablespoon of the pork mixture in the center of each disk.
Fold the dough over the filling and press the edges together to seal the bun.
Place the buns on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and let them rise in a warm place for 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees and bake the buns for 18 minutes, or until they are golden brown.
Brush the tops of the buns with sesame oil and sprinkle with chopped scallions.
Serve the buns warm and enjoy.
Cook pork to an internal temperature of 63°C / 145°F, then rest 3 minutes before serving.
